MR TIMOTHY LAM JR: Mr J C H Ho (Stipendiary Steward)
ALMIGHTY WARRIOR: Near the 1000 Metres was steadied to avoid HAPPY PEGASUS.  After improving to the inside of HAPPY PEGASUS (C L Chau) leaving the 500 Metres was then steadied when HAPPY PEGASUS shifted in.  C L Chau was advised to exercise more care.
JEDI SPURS: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead.  She said having regard to her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages to ensure JEDI SPURS showed sufficient pace to cross runners to its inside.  She said after obtaining a margin in advance of HAPPY PEGASUS in the early stages she then commenced to restrain her mount when she was satisfied that JEDI SPURS would be able to lead as instructed.  She said as she commenced to restrain her mount approaching the 1000 Metres JEDI SPURS raced keenly and would not respond to her efforts to set a slower pace.  She said making the turn leaving the 900 Metres as she applied more pressure to steady the horse to set a more sustainable pace JEDI SPURS became unbalanced when it got its head up and shifted out and from this point she was unable to control the horse in the lead.  She added that soon after entering the Home Straight JEDI SPURS came under pressure before giving ground noticeably over the final 200 Metres.  Trainer D A Hayes advised the horse had pleased him leading into the race and was of the opinion JEDI SPURS raced too keenly, particularly when ridden along in the early stages to go forward.  He added that he would now place a hood on the horse for its next race start and use the services of a senior rider.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  The performance of JEDI SPURS was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, JEDI SPURS will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

He added when SPEEDY POWER quickened near the 250 Metres his mount took some time to respond to his riding and after laying in and away from PRIVATE WEALTH when obtaining a narrow run between PRIVATE WEALTH and COPARTNER A I near the 100 Metres he was satisfied with his mount’s finishing effort over the concluding stages.

MR COOL: Near the 400 Metres was bumped by FLASH CURRENT which attempted to shift out.  When questioned K Teetan stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable but not to ride it along in the early stages.  He said those instructions were issued as MR COOL had not finished its races off last season when ridden in a forward position.  He said at its last start win on 4 October 2026 MR COOL was able to obtain a handy position without being ridden along to do so and his intention was to ride the horse in a similar manner today.  He said whilst MR COOL jumped well he was of the opinion he would have had to make too much use of the horse in the early stages to cross runners to his inside and for this reason he elected to restrain his mount to attempt to obtain a position with cover behind PRESTIGE COME.  He said when GENIUS BABY and GRAND PATCH improved to his inside he was unable to obtain cover and as a result was obliged to race very wide and without cover in the early stages.  He said as the pace of the event was being run outside of standard time he then elected to ride MR COOL forward from the 900 Metres to cross GRAND PATCH where he then raced wide and without cover for the remainder of the middle stages.  Trainer F C Lor confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with the ride of Jockey Teetan.  After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Teetan that he had made an error of judgement in the early stages in not attempting to cross runners to his inside, particularly when MR COOL had jumped well and the early and middle stages of the event were being run outside of standard time.

KING ZOOM: Slow to begin. He said when ROAD TO GLORY did not improve into the race as he had expected he then shifted to the inside of that runner near the 300 Metres to secure clear running.  He added that his mount then commenced to finish the race off well but over the final 100 Metres could not be ridden out when it improved close to FLASH CURRENT.  The Stewards advised Jockey Orman that, in their opinion, he had made an error of judgement in not improving to the inside of ROAD TO GLORY sooner than what he did to ensure that his mount was provided with the first available opportunity to improve.

AWESOME FLUKE: When questioned Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward and lead if circumstances permitted.  She said in accordance with her instructions she rode her mount along in the early stages, however, AWESOME FLUKE took some time to muster speed which resulted in a number of runners crossing her mount in the early stages.  She said when left without cover near the 1400 Metres AWESOME FLUKE then commenced to race keenly and her intention was to endeavour to obtain a position with cover behind DEFINITIVE.  She said when CALIFORNIATOTALITY maintained its position one-off behind DEFINITIVE, this resulted in AWESOME FLUKE being obliged to race wide and without cover.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to go forward from the 1300 Metres having regard to the early stages being run outside of standard time, Apprentice Yuen agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect she had made an error of judgement in not allowing her mount to stride forward, particularly as it was racing keenly.  She added that when positioned to the outside of DEFINITIVE she was mindful not to crowd runners to her inside and for this reason she remained racing three wide and without cover from the 900 Metres and into the Home Straight.  Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions were to go forward and agreed with the Stewards that in retrospect Apprentice Yuen should have taken the initiative to go forward and cross DEFINITIVE.  When questioned regarding the tactics adopted on the stablemate CHILL EASY, Mr Yiu advised that he had expected the horse to hold a midfield position and was surprised that AWESOME FLUKE remained three deep during the race, particularly from barrier 6 having regard to the instructions.  He said it was not the intention of the stable for this to occur and in the circumstances it was Apprentice Yuen’s riding which led to CHILL EASY being able to obtain cover behind AWESOME FLUKE.
